reasons: **Crew stays just under the heat safety line, with almost no room to spare.** Even for the workers who heat up most, body temperature tops out at about 37.9 °C against a 38.0 °C limit. A small surprise, like a hotter afternoon or a slow break, could push someone over, so watch the crew closely and enforce breaks.
**Kofi is kept off the heaviest jobs in the hottest hours.** He's new and his body isn't used to working in this heat yet, so he gets lighter tasks during peak heat. Others pick up that heavy work.

**This plan gets the most done while running the coolest.** It completes about 80% of the most important work. Spreading the heavy work evenly across everyone gets the same amount done but runs the crew slightly hotter. A "balanced" plan does a little less (79%) and runs hotter still. None of the options finishes everything without risking overheating.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
